title: Pairing order and condensate fraction across the BCS-BEC crossover in the two-dimensional attractive Hubbard model
authors: Hao Du, Qian Sun, Zhuotao Xie, Yuan-Yao He
abstract: We report a systematic study of the superconducting ground state in the two-dimensional attractive Hubbard model, employing the {\it numerically exact} auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method. We focus primarily on the pairing order and condensate fraction across the BCS-BEC crossover. Our numerical calculations cover a broad and physically relevant parameter regime, with the interaction strength $U/t=2\sim 12$ (where $t$ is the nearest-neighbor hopping amplitude) and fermion density $n=0.25\sim 1.0$. We systematically characterize the dependence of the pairing order and condensate fraction on both the interaction strength and fermion density, and perform finite-size extrapolations to obtain their thermodynamic-limit values. As complementary quantities, we also provide high-precision numerical results for the double occupancy and total energy. Furthermore, we investigate the effects of next-nearest-neighbor hopping on the superconducting properties of the model. Our results offer a comprehensive set of unbiased numerical data for the attractive Hubbard model, establishing quantitative benchmarks for understanding superconductivity across the BCS-BEC crossover and for validating future theoretical and numerical approaches.
summary: This paper uses the Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo method to study the superconducting ground state of the 2D attractive Hubbard model across the BCS-BEC crossover. It calculates key quantities like pairing order and condensate fraction over a broad range of interaction strengths and densities. The work provides essential, high-precision numerical benchmarks for theoretical models describing unconventional superconductivity.
main_problem: The study systematically investigates the superconducting ground state and the evolution of pairing order and condensate fraction across the BCS-BEC crossover.
main_result: The research provides a comprehensive set of unbiased numerical data for the attractive Hubbard model, establishing quantitative benchmarks for understanding superconductivity across the BCS-BEC crossover.
method: The primary method employed is the numerically exact Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) technique, which is used to project the ground state.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the two-dimensional (2D) attractive Hubbard model on a square lattice. The Hamiltonian includes nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor hopping terms and an attractive interaction $U$.
key_observables: Pairing order, condensate fraction, double occupancy, and total energy density.
important_parameters: Interaction strength $U/t$ (ranging from 2 to 12) and fermion density $n$ (ranging from 0.25 to 1.0).
main_assumptions: The study relies on finite-size extrapolations to obtain thermodynamic-limit values, utilizing advanced boundary condition techniques (TABC) to mitigate finite-size effects.
figures_summary: Figures compare numerical results for pairing order ($\langle\Delta^2angle$) and condensate fraction ($n_c$) obtained under Periodic Boundary Conditions (PBC) versus Twist-Averaged Boundary Conditions (TABC), demonstrating the necessity of the latter for accurate extrapolation.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the superconducting ground state by calculating key observables across a wide parameter space, detailing the computational methodology (AFQMC) and addressing the convergence issues associated with finite-size effects.
why_interesting: The rigorous numerical benchmarking of the BCS-BEC crossover in a lattice model is highly relevant for understanding pairing mechanisms in strongly correlated materials, which often bridge the gap between weak-coupling BCS theory and strong-coupling BEC regimes.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Benchmark comparison between AFQMC and ED for (a) the total energy density e/t and double occupancy D, and (b) the mean-squared pairing order ⟨ˆ∆2⟩and condensate fraction nc, as functions of the interaction strength U/t for the standard 2D attractive Hubbard model (1) on an L = 4 system with PBC. The fermion density is n = 0.625. The insets show the differences between the AFQMC and ED re- sults for the corresponding observables, with ED taken as the reference.

FIG. 2. Momentum distribution n(k) and k-space pair wave function ϕ↑↓(k) along the high-symmetry path Γ →X →M →Γ in the Brillouin zone for three interaction strengths: (a) U/t = 2, (b) U/t = 6, and (c) U/t = 12. The fermion density is n = 0.875 in all three panels. The left and right y-axis scales and tick labels are identical for all panels. Vertical cyan dashed lines indicate the noninteracting Fermi surface, which is shown in the inset of panel (a) within the quarter Brillouin zone. The calculations are performed with L = 24 under PBC for the standard 2D attractive Hubbard model (1).

FIG. 3. Momentum distribution n(k) and k-space pair wave function ϕ↑↓(k) along the high-symmetry path Γ →X →M →Γ in the Brillouin zone for three fermion densities: (a) n = 1.0, (b) n = 0.5, and (c) n = 0.25. The interaction strength is U/t = 12 in all three panels. The left and right y-axis scales and tick labels are identical for all panels. Vertical cyan dashed lines indicate the noninteracting Fermi surface, which is shown in the inset of each panel within the quarter Brillouin zone. The calculations are performed with L = 24 under PBC for the standard 2D attractive Hubbard model (1).

FIG. 4. The r-space pair wave function ψ↑↓(r) as a function of |r| along the diagonal direction [r = (x, x)] for (a) n = 0.875 with U/t = 2, 6, 12, and (b) U/t = 12 with n = 1.0, 0.5, 0.25. The solid lines are spline interpolations of the AFQMC data points. Panels (a) and (b) correspond to the results shown in Figs. 2 and 3, respectively, and are also obtained with L = 24.

FIG. 6. Finite-size extrapolations of (a) condensate fraction nc, and (b) mean-squared pairing order ⟨∆2⟩and pair-pair correlations P[r = (L/2, L/2)] and P[r = (L/2, 0)], versus 1/L for the standard 2D attractive Hubbard model (1) under PBC. In panel (a), three sets of parameters are shown: (U/t = 12, n = 0.375), (U/t = 8, n = 0.625), and (U/t = 4, n = 1.0), with the data for the latter two shifted by +0.1 and +0.3, respectively, for clarity. In panel (b), the parameter set (U/t = 6, n = 0.625) is used. The solid lines represent least- squares fits to the AFQMC data using quadratic polynomials in 1/L. The corresponding TDL values obtained from the extrapolations are also included.
